nodes.label: deepgram.png (Deepgram Provider Icon Asset)
nodes.description: Static brand/identity asset served from the frontend public dir. 128x128 PNG, 2736 bytes, 8-bit RGBA. It carries no data payload, no UI layout, no text content: it is purely a visual mark used to identify a provider entry in lists, cards, headers and topology graphs.

nodes.label: AI Letter Monogram Mark
nodes.description: Bold black stylized 'AI' letterform, the A and I interlocked/kerned as a single ligature, centered on a white rounded-square tile filling the full 128x128 canvas. Pure black glyph on light background, no gradients, no color accent, no enclosing frame beyond the tile's own rounded corners. Ambiguity: the mark is the two letters 'AI' only; nothing in the asset ties the letterform to a specific vendor wordmark, so whether it is a brand-accurate Deepgram mark or a generic letter monogram within the tile set cannot be determined from the image alone.
nodes.ambiguity: Cannot verify from the asset whether 'AI' is Deepgram's own wordmark or a generic letter monogram used across the provider tile set.

nodes.label: Deepgram (Speech AI Provider)
nodes.rationale: The asset filename names the vendor explicitly, and the frontend provider registry (frontend/src/shared/constants/providers.js, id 'deepgram', alias 'dg', brand color #13EF93) shows Deepgram is a real supported provider, not an asset-only stub. Note the registry carries a brand color (#13EF93) and a lucide 'mic' icon plus textIcon 'DG' fallback, while this tile is monochrome 'AI' lettering - i.e. the icon asset and the in-code brand identity are two parallel, non-derivable representations of the same vendor.

nodes.label: Provider ID PNG Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Every consumer in the frontend builds the asset URL by string interpolation, e.g. src={`/providers/${providerId}.png`} (Header.jsx, ModelSelectModal.jsx, media-providers pages, usage ProviderLimits cards, ProviderTopology.jsx, automation page, DefaultToolCard.jsx). Because the lookup is a raw template literal with no manifest or import map, the on-disk filename must be character-identical to the provider id, otherwise the request 404s and the onError handler sets display:none, silently rendering no icon at all. This is why an asset can exist with no import statement anywhere in the codebase yet still be load-bearing.

nodes.label: 128px Monochrome Provider Icon Tile Pattern
nodes.rationale: This asset belongs to a set of 106 sibling tiles in frontend/public/providers, all 128x128 (verified groq.png, assemblyai.png, azure.png match the same 128x128 canvas), each holding one high-contrast dark glyph or wordmark on a light background. Consumers render them at roughly 20px (className 'size-5 rounded object-contain') inside dense pickers, tables and status cards. The single-glyph-on-light rule is a legibility trade-off: a 20px box cannot resolve a full-color brand logo, so identity is reduced to the most distinctive letterform, and the uniform 128px canvas keeps the grid visually even when marks differ in intrinsic ink coverage.
